dedupe_keys.name: arcep bottom up cost model of an efficient generic mobile operator metropole and overseas

description: Arcep's technical and economic model of the network costs of a generic efficient mobile operator is a bottom-up cost model that the French regulator uses to set mobile call termination rates. Arcep put a first version out for public consultation from 8 October to 20 November 2013, publishing the model itself as a spreadsheet package (a zip file of about 22 MB) with its documentation, so that operators and other parties could inspect and test it. An updated model followed on 12 September 2014 (a zip file of 22,055,559 bytes). The model covers three areas with their own geography and traffic: metropolitan France, the Antilles and French Guiana, and Réunion and Mayotte. It dimensions the radio access, transmission and core networks of a generic operator from coverage and traffic demand and calculates the incremental cost of voice termination and other services. Coverage: France including overseas departments. Format and access: downloadable spreadsheet model and PDF documents on the Arcep site, in French, free. Caveats: parameters reflect 2013 to 2014 assumptions; the modelled operator is hypothetical, not any real network. Simulation uses: cost-based economic appraisal of mobile network deployment and interconnection pricing, including island networks, and a worked example of dimensioning rules. Related records: the Bundesnetzagentur mobile and broadband cost models are German counterparts, and the ANFR and Arcep station data describe real French networks.
